summary: Richard “Dick” Uihlein co-founded Uline with his wife, Elizabeth, and is the private company's chairman. The fortune generated by Uline has made him one of the largest Republican donors in the United States, with unusually sustained funding for candidate-specific super PACs, state judicial races and a network centered on Restoration PAC and Restoration of America.

chapters.title: Family and formation
chapters.dek: A business dynasty and an inherited political tradition
chapters.body:
Richard Uihlein was born in 1945 into a German-American family whose earlier fortune came from Milwaukee's Schlitz brewing company. His father, Edgar Uihlein Jr., ran a plastics business and funded right-wing organizations; Richard later said his father shaped his own conservatism [[propublica-box-empire-2022]].

He married Elizabeth before graduating from Stanford in 1967, then joined the family business. The inheritance was cultural and financial, but the much larger fortune that later financed their politics came from the company the couple built together [[propublica-box-empire-2022, forbes-richard-2026]].

chapters.title: Building Uline
chapters.dek: A basement distributor becomes a private industrial-supply giant
chapters.body:
In 1980, Richard and Elizabeth started Uline from their basement after identifying demand for a local shipping-supply distributor. Its first signature product was a carton sizer; the catalog expanded into packaging, material-handling, safety and industrial supplies [[uline-history]].

Uline remains privately held. Its official history lists Elizabeth as chief executive and Richard as chairman, with their children in senior roles. Forbes estimated more than 9,000 employees and billions in annual revenue, making ownership of the company the basis of Richard's wealth [[uline-history, forbes-richard-2026]].

chapters.title: From donor to megadonor
chapters.dek: Unlimited outside spending changes the scale
chapters.body:
Uihlein gave politically for years, but his spending rose sharply during the super-PAC era. By 2018 he had given more than $38 million to conservative candidates and groups in a single federal cycle, second among pro-Republican individual donors only to Sheldon Adelson [[wapo-richard-2018, propublica-immigration-2019]].

His public explanation is ideological rather than transactional: he has named free speech, free markets, smaller government, gun rights and opposition to abortion as priorities. Those commitments help explain the range of recipients, while the contribution record—not the recipient's every position—defines what he personally supported [[wapo-richard-2018]].

chapters.title: The Restoration network
chapters.dek: Long-term funding builds institutions as well as campaigns
chapters.body:
Restoration PAC became the most durable vehicle in Uihlein's political network. ProPublica identified him as its primary funder and traced its spending into voter-file projects, advertising and organizations linked to Restoration of America [[fec-restoration, propublica-voteref-2022]].

The network also funded media operations that produced partisan local-style publications. ProPublica reported that Uihlein had supplied about $125 million to Restoration PAC since 2020; that figure describes funding to the committee, not proof that he directed each downstream expenditure [[propublica-catholic-tribune-2024]].

chapters.title: National Republican politics
chapters.dek: Large checks across presidential and congressional contests
chapters.body:
During the 2016 primary Uihlein first backed Scott Walker and Ted Cruz, then supported pro-Trump groups after Donald Trump became the nominee. His later federal giving mixed Trump-aligned committees with groups focused on congressional races and ideological primary challengers [[nyt-uihleins-2018, fec-richard]].

The couple's combined disclosed giving reached another scale in 2024. OpenSecrets counted approximately $143.5 million from Richard and Elizabeth, all on the Republican side in its cycle classification. Their individual ledgers must remain separate even when rankings describe them as one household [[opensecrets-2024]].

chapters.title: State races as laboratories
chapters.dek: Governors, courts, schools and ballot measures
chapters.body:
Uihlein has repeatedly placed large bets in state politics: Bruce Rauner in Illinois, Darren Bailey's 2022 challenge to J.B. Pritzker, Wisconsin judicial contests and conservative candidates far beyond the states where he lives or works [[suntimes-uihlein-2017, propublica-box-empire-2022, wpr-court-2025]].

The pattern continued in 2026 with $17 million for a California voter-identification ballot campaign. In a Wisconsin congressional primary, Richard and Elizabeth funded opposing candidates, evidence that their joint business and broad partisan alignment do not make every political choice identical [[sfchronicle-prop39-2026, ap-wisconsin-primary-2026]].

chapters.title: Where business and politics meet
chapters.dek: Company policy, lobbying and public positions
chapters.body:
Uline's scale gives the family influence apart from campaign checks. The company has lobbied on transportation rules that affect its distribution business, while the Uihleins supported candidates and organizations involved in the same policy environment [[atlantic-duffy-2026]].

A 2019 visa dispute illustrates the need for precision. Uline challenged the denial of a specialized visa for a Mexican employee and withdrew its suit after a later petition succeeded. ProPublica contrasted the case with restrictionist candidates Uihlein funded, but it did not establish illegality by Uline or a change in his public immigration position [[propublica-immigration-2019]].

chapters.title: Present influence
chapters.dek: A private company finances a public political infrastructure
chapters.body:
Richard Uihlein's influence comes from the combination of a continuing private-company fortune and repeat funding. Candidate bets can lose—Darren Bailey did—but institutions such as Restoration PAC persist between elections and redirect money into later races and advocacy [[propublica-box-empire-2022, fec-restoration]].

As of October 2026, he remains Uline's chairman and an active federal and state donor. The FEC ledger is a lower bound: it omits state committees, ballot measures and nonprofit transfers, while household totals can obscure which spouse made each choice [[uline-history, fec-richard, sfchronicle-prop39-2026]].
